Assume the hard part is solved: the thing is reliable, it doesn't leak your data, and it does exactly what you'd have done (in a perfect world I'm creating). Which task goes first? Sorting files, drafting replies, blocking the calendar, paying the bills, deleting old stuff, following up on people who haven't answered. Or what?

I've been thinking about this because I've noticed that the tasks I'd hand over aren't the ones that take the most time. They're the ones I dread starting. Filing takes ten minutes and I'd give it up to tomorrow. Writing a hard email takes ten minutes too but I would never let anything else do it, even flawlessly, because the doing is the point.

So there seems to be a category of work that's about the outcome and a category that's about the person doing it, and I'm curious where other people draw that line. What would you automate without a second thought at all, and what would you keep even if keeping it made you slower? I'm interested in the reasons more than the lists.
